Quick read and finance take:
- We modeled the scenarios. If we do a simple rebate credit tied to GPU index >25% (cap rebate at 40% of the delta), worst-case exposure over 24 months is ~8% of committed revenue in a highly adverse GPU spike scenario (see tab 'stress' in the spreadsheet).
- We can approve a standard rebate clause (up to the 40% cap) at the Sales Director level. Anything that increases the cap or moves to an up-front discounted credit >10% needs VP Finance approval.
- For deeper structural discounts (15%+ on committed spend), this requires a commercial exception and mark-to-market clauses (legal + finance sign-off).

Gapped items: we need legal to weigh in on precise indexation language and whether a rebate is a credit applied monthly vs. a settlement at quarter close. Operationally, monthly credits can be automated but will require small bookkeeping work.

Regards,

High level (finalizable):
- Term: 24 months (Jan 1, 2027 — Dec 31, 2028).
- Reserved pool: 120 reserved GPU‑equivalents (mix A100/RTX per SOW).
- Pricing: baseline unit price per GPU = $X (see spreadsheet attached).
- Rebate structure (Option A): quarterly rebate credit if Redwood GPU index > 20% vs baseline in the quarter. Rebate = min( (index_delta * 0.6) * committed_spend_in_quarter, cap = 40% of index_delta exposure ). Rebate applied as account credit in the following billing cycle.
- Approvals: Sales Director can approve the standard rebate capped at 40% exposure. Legal will finalize indexation wording and monthly vs quarterly settlement.
- Operational note: we will define a three‑quarter soft ramp in the SOW to match NovaMed's provisioning plan; Jonas confirmed allocation is feasible without impacting existing commitments.
